Multiplexed analysis of projections by sequencing (MAPseq) showed that most superficial collicular neurons project to a single downstream target, but target probabilities differ between upper- and lower-field populations. Together, these findings identify visual-field position as a major organizing principle of input and output connectivity in the superficial superior colliculus.

title: Threat-induced behavioral plasticity in two invertebrate chordates integrates sensory and neuromodulatory inputs.
abstract: Threat detection and evasion are fundamental challenges across the animal kingdom. Here, we examine threat detection and avoidance behaviors in two planktonic tunicates, Ciona intestinalis larvae and Oikopleura dioica adults, by quantifying locomotion and ecologically relevant behaviors in the presence of copepods. Both species exhibited marked increases in swimming speed, distance traveled, and roaming behavior upon predator exposure, whereas conditioned water alone had no effect. Despite this shared response, behavioral organization diverged: C. intestinalis primarily reallocated time toward roaming with few state transitions, while O. dioica increased behavioral switching, reduced dwelling, and prolonged roaming bouts. Pharmacological manipulations revealed species-specific effects of compounds targeting monoaminergic, glutamatergic, and GABAergic signaling: in C. intestinalis, bioamine, glutamatergic, and GABAergic perturbations disrupted threat-induced movement patterning, whereas in O. dioica they suppressed motility increases. Predator presence also accelerated metamorphosis and altered settlement in C. intestinalis, while in O. dioica it triggered rapid house escape, delayed expansion, and reduced turnover. Finally, we show that C. intestinalis larvae leverage a network of polymodal sensory neurons to detect chemical cues emanating from the copepods. Whole-brain calcium imaging suggested that these cues engage widespread yet structured neural activity across the larval brain, recruiting distributed neuronal populations with distinct temporal response motifs. Circuit-level analysis further indicated that sensory inputs propagate through a hierarchical sensorimotor network linking peripheral neurons to central interneurons and motor outputs, supporting a distributed transformation of threat-related information into behavior. These findings uncover conserved yet mechanistically distinct antipredator strategies in two evolutionarily distant tunicates.

title: Mechanisms involved in the sex-dependent dopaminergic neurodegeneration induced by MDMA in a mouse model of adolescent drug exposure.
abstract: 3,4-Methylenedioxymethamphetamine (MDMA, or "ecstasy") is an amphetamine-related drug mainly used by adolescents. Studies in mice have demonstrated that MDMA administration induces toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system, some of which may be sex- and age-dependent. Since adolescence is a critical period for brain development, this study aimed to investigate some of the mechanisms underlying MDMA-induced toxicity in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system of adolescent mice. Male and female adolescent mice were treated with a regimen of MDMA (4 × 20 mg/kg, 2 h apart) that has previously been demonstrated to induce toxic effects in the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system. After treatment, mice were sacrificed at different time points (i.e., 30, 60 or 120 min) to evaluate loss of nigral dopaminergic neurons, antioxidant and proteasome activity, reactive radical species (RRS) and neurodegeneration-related proteins. Immunohistochemistry for tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) was performed in the substantia nigra pars compacta (SNc). Moreover, midbrains were evaluated for: i) activity of the antioxidant enzymes glutathione peroxidase (GPx) and superoxide dismutase (SOD) 1 and 2 of the proteolytic subunits β2 trypsin-like and β5 chymotrypsin-like of the proteasome system; ii) expression of SOD1 and SOD2 genes; iii) presence of RRS and iv) phosphorylation of the extracellular signal-regulated kinase (ERK1/2) and of the signal transducer and activator of transcription 3 (STAT3). Male mice displayed: i) decreased TH immunoreactivity and cresyl violet staining (120 min after the last MDMA administration); ii) reduced activity of SOD and β2 trypsin-like proteasome subunit, both in basal conditions and 120 min after the last MDMA administration; iii) increase in p-ERK1/2 (30 min after the last MDMA administration). Female mice treated with MDMA displayed: i) decreased SOD1 and SOD2 gene expression and ii) increased GPx activity (both observed 120 min after the last MDMA administration). MDMA treatment during adolescence altered the homeostasis of the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system in both male and female mice. Adolescent male mice treated with MDMA appeared more sensitive to dysfunction in proteasome and ERK1/2 activation. Conversely, female mice efficiently maintained the antioxidant activity, which could contrast the neurotoxic effects of MDMA on the nigrostriatal dopaminergic system.

title: From Gene Sets to Brain Function: A Physiology-Informed Framework for Multi-Omics Integration in Precision Neurophysiology.
abstract: Public omics repositories and multi-omics technologies have substantially expanded the molecular characterization of chronic human diseases by enabling large-scale analyses across diverse biological and clinical contexts. However, in neurological disorders, translating omics-derived associations into mechanistic insight and clinical relevance remains challenging due to the dynamic and multiscale nature of brain function. Gene set-based analytical approaches effectively identify enriched molecular patterns, but are limited in capturing temporal dynamics, network-level interactions, and physiological state dependence that define neural systems. This conceptual methodological review synthesizes foundational infrastructure papers, methodological evaluations, and translational neuroscience literature to critically examine the application of public omics resources in human neurophysiology, focusing on the interpretive gap between molecular-level associations and functional brain processes. We examine major public omics infrastructures, widely used gene set analysis frameworks, the principal strategies for multi-omics integration, and the challenge of batch effects in public data reuse, highlighting both their analytical strengths and structural limitations. Core neurophysiological principles, including synaptic transmission, network dynamics, plasticity, and homeostatic regulation, are discussed to clarify why direct inference from static molecular profiles to brain function is inherently constrained. Clinical illustrations from epilepsy, attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder, and migraine demonstrate how chronic neurological disorders emerge from context-dependent neural dynamics that are not readily reducible to gene set-level summaries. Finally, we outline future directions for integrating artificial intelligence with public omics resources, emphasizing physiology-informed modeling, explainable AI, and ethical considerations to support more interpretable and translational precision health strategies in chronic neurological disease.

title: Pathways to progress: navigating the evolving field of PIDs and associated conditions - proceedings from the IPOPI Global Multi-Stakeholders' Summit (July 2025).
abstract: In July 2025, the International Patient Organisation for Primary Immunodeficiencies (IPOPI) held its fourth consecutive Global Multi-Stakeholders' Summit, bringing together key stakeholders and experts in primary immunodeficiencies (PIDs) and related fields to discuss current challenges and opportunities for improving patient care. This edition focused on current and projected trends to 2035 in artificial intelligence and quantum computing, the gap between primary and secondary immunodeficiencies, and the role of preventive medicine in patients' quality of life. Stakeholders from all around the world gathered to examine current knowledge gaps, needs and avenues to improve the care of patients with immunodeficiency in the next ten years. Recommendations on how digital technologies can contribute to equitable access to innovative therapies are proposed. Mechanisms by which multidisciplinary teams can work together to improve the care of patients with immunodeficiencies are outlined, including how innovative screening and care plans can reduce the risk of multiorgan involvement and complications in these patients. Within the next decade, digital tools in conjunction with improved multistakeholder collaborations is most likely to contribute to the collection of standardised data, inclusive studies, and personalised treatments that will prolong, with quality, the lives of patients with immunodeficiencies.

title: Subtle microglia and oligodendrocyte precursor cell histological changes across social stress paradigms.
abstract: Social stress is a key risk factor for disorders of increased aversion responsiveness, and changes in cortico-limbic oligodendrocyte lineage and myelination may contribute to this pathological process. In adult male mice, we demonstrated previously that social stress-induced aversion hyper-responsiveness co-occurs with altered oligodendrocyte proliferation-maturation dynamics and myelin content. Overall, however, findings on these inter-relationships are inconsistent across studies using various stress paradigms, suggesting that there is not a simple relationship between social stress and the extent and direction (i.e., loss vs. gain) of changes in the oligodendrocyte lineage and myelin. Under physiological conditions, the immune cells of the CNS, microglia, monitor the CNS microenvironment and contribute to oligodendrocyte lineage and myelin homeostasis. Also, recent reports suggest that microglia state might influence oligodendrocyte lineage changes in response to certain social stress paradigms. Here, we begin to address the hypothesis that social stress induced changes in microglia and oligodendrocyte lineage are inter-related in mice. We employed histological and semi-automated image analyses to characterize a subset of microglia and OPC histological properties in medial prefrontal cortex (mPFC) and basal amygdala (BA) following aversive social experiences, including chronic social stress (CSS), CSS followed by aversion learning (excessive aversive stimulation), and social isolation (as the absence of sociopositive stimulation). Specifically, we assessed: (1) the density and proliferation rate of microglia and OPCs; (2) the spatial relationship between microglia and OPCs; and (3) microglia morphological complexity as a proxy for their activity/state. The preliminary integrative histological evidence is for subtle stress paradigm-associated alterations in microglia- and OPC-related features, and limited correlative histological associations between these cell populations.

title: Associations of vision, audition, and motor function with cognition from midlife to advanced age.
journal: International journal of clinical and health psychology : IJCHP
abstract: Vision, audition, and motor function are closely interrelated, complicating the attribution of their cognitive associations to individual functions. We examined their individual and joint relationships with five cognitive domains in 455 adults aged 36-100 years from the Lifespan Human Connectome Project in Aging. Analyses assessed each function after accounting for the other two, their combined associations with cognition, and their contribution to cognitive prediction. Associations were examined across the full age range and within early midlife, late midlife, and older adulthood. Older age was associated with poorer sensory, motor, and fluid cognitive performance. Vision was associated with working memory, episodic memory, executive function, and language across all participants, although the corresponding associations were not detected within the separate age groups in the primary analyses. Auditory associations involved language in early midlife and working memory in late midlife, with a broader range observed in older adulthood. Motor function was most consistently associated with executive function, with this relationship detected in all three groups. Formal comparisons did not establish differences in association strength between age groups after correction for multiple comparisons. Combined sensory and motor performance was associated with all five cognitive domains. The distinction between individual and combined associations was clearest for processing speed, which was associated with combined performance in all three age groups but with none of the individual functions after mutual adjustment in the primary analyses. Adding sensory and motor measures to models containing age and sex improved cross-validated prediction for four cognitive domains, with the largest improvement for executive function. These findings characterize distinct patterns of association between sensory and motor function and higher cognitive abilities, underscoring the importance of considering these interrelated functions jointly from midlife to advanced age.

title: Cheek Characteristics and Their Relationship with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
abstract: To investigate whether cheek appearance, posture, mobility, and pressure are associated with the presence and severity of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) in adults. Te currents cross-sectional study included 100 adults aged 18 to 59 years, classified as controls or as having mild, moderate, or severe OSA based on type-I polysomnography. Cheek appearance/posture and mobility were assessed using the Expanded Protocol of Orofacial Myofunctional Evaluation with Scores, and cheek pressure was measured using the Iowa Oral Performance Instrument (model 2.2; IOPI Medical LLC). Descriptive statistics, Spearman's correlation tests, Mann-Whitney tests, and multiple linear regression were performed at a significance level of 5%. The apnea-hypopnea index (AHI) was positively correlated with the body mass index (BMI) and negatively correlated with cheek appearance/posture scores, whereas cheek mobility and cheek pressure were not significantly correlated with the AHI. Across OSA severity groups, cheek appearance/posture scores differed significantly: individuals with moderate and severe OSA had lower scores than the controls. No significant between-group differences were observed for cheek mobility or pressure. In the multivariable analyses, the BMI was the only variable independently associated with the AHI. Neither cheek appearance/posture nor cheek mobility remained independently associated with the AHI after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI, and cheek pressure was also not independently associated with the AHI in the secondary model. Cheek appearance/posture was associated with OSA severity in the unadjusted analyses, but it did not remain independently associated with the AHI after adjustment for age, sex, and BMI. Cheek mobility and pressure showed limited associations with OSA severity.

title: miR-132-3p-Enriched Exosomes Modulate Axonal and Mitochondrial Markers in Middle Cerebral Artery Occlusion Rats.
abstract: Ischemic stroke causes substantial neurological disability, but effective neural repair strategies remain limited. Mesenchymal stem/stromal cell (MSC)-derived exosomes may offer therapeutic potential because of their low toxicity, limited immunogenicity, and ability to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB). Among their bioactive cargo, miR-132-3p is implicated in axonal growth and neuronal survival. This study aimed to investigate whether miR-132- 3p-enriched exosomes improve early outcomes and modulate axonal and mitochondrial markers after experimental ischemic stroke. In this randomized experimental animal study, 115 adult male Wistar rats were assigned to the sham, middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO), exosome-treated (Exo), or miR-132-3p-enriched exosometreated (Exo-miR-132) groups (n=5 per group). Focal ischemia was induced by 90 minutes of intraluminal MCAO. Human umbilical cord MSC-derived exosomes were isolated by differential ultracentrifugation and characterized using transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, Western blotting, and flow cytometry. miR-132-3p was loaded into exosomes by electroporation, with the optimal concentration selected based on brain Nefh expression. Animals received Exo or Exo-miR-132 intravenously at 0 and 24 hours after MCAO. At 48 hours, six behavioral assessments were performed. Infarct volume, BBB permeability, brain water content, and neuronal cell death were assessed, whereas axonal and mitochondrial markers were evaluated by immunofluorescence. Exosomes showed characteristic morphology and expressed CD9, CD63, and CD81. The 5-nmol loading concentration produced the greatest increase in brain Nefh expression. Compared with Exo, Exo-miR-132 was associated with higher NF-H and mitofusin-2 expression and lower peptidyl-prolyl cis-trans isomerase D, cytochrome c, dynamin-1-like protein, and p21 expression. Exo-miR-132 also reduced infarct volume, BBB permeability, cerebral edema, neuronal cell death, and neurological deficits, with greater effects than Exo for several outcomes. miR-132-3p-enriched exosomes modulated axonal regeneration-associated markers and mitochondrial fission/fusion balance, alongside reduced injury and improved early neurological outcomes. Direct evidence of axonal regrowth and long-term functional recovery requires further investigation.

title: Sprint National Anaesthesia Project 3: A survey of perioperative medicine services for older surgical patients in Australia.
abstract: Increasing numbers of older people with age-related conditions such as frailty and multimorbidity are presenting for surgical procedures, which is associated with an increased risk of postoperative complications. This study aimed to assess the provision of perioperative medicine services for older surgical patients across Australian hospitals participating in the third Sprint National Anaesthesia Project. An organisational survey was conducted involving 23 Australian hospitals, collecting data on hospital characteristics, clinical governance, preoperative assessments (including frailty, cognition, and risk of delirium), and postoperative care practices for high-risk older patients. Responses were analysed to evaluate the structure and function of perioperative services for older surgical patients. Twenty-one hospitals completed the survey. Preoperative assessments of older surgical patients were predominantly nurse- or anaesthetist-led, with limited geriatrician involvement. Routine preoperative screening of frailty and cognition was rare, and there was significant variability in approaches to the assessment of postoperative delirium. The survey highlights inconsistencies in perioperative care delivery for older surgical patients, revealing gaps in the implementation of established guidelines and recommendations. There is a need for a structured approach to integrate geriatric services into surgical pathways, with an emphasis on routine screening for frailty, cognitive impairment, multimorbidity, and delirium.

title: LRRK2 in Focus: A Global Browser Linking Genetic Diversity to Functional Effects.
journal: Movement disorders : official journal of the Movement Disorder Society
abstract: LRRK2 (leucine-rich repeat kinase 2) variants are major contributors to Parkinson's disease (PD). Many pathogenic variants increase kinase activity, underscoring the value of functional assays in nominating therapeutic targets such as kinase inhibitors. The objective of this study was to develop an interactive resource that provides functional context and ancestry-specific variant frequencies. Genetic data were analyzed for 116,923 individuals (71,905 PD, 45,018 controls) from the Global Parkinson's Genetics Program (GP2) and integrated with clinical and in vitro biochemical kinase activity information. The LRRK2 Browser (http://gp2.org/lrrk2browser) displays genetic data for 22,172 LRRK2 variants (1031 exonic, 12 disease-associated) across 11 populations and functional data for 179 variants. Clinical annotations include age, age at onset, and family history of PD. The publicly available LRRK2 Browser represents an open-access resource to support LRRK2 variant interpretation. It aims to enhance the translational potential of genetic and functional data for precision medicine and the implementation of gene-targeted therapies in diverse populations. © 2026 The Author(s). Movement Disorders published by Wiley Periodicals LLC on behalf of International Parkinson and Movement Disorder Society.

title: Neurovascular Unit Redox-Metabolic Communication in Poststroke Cognitive Impairment: Spatiotemporal Dysregulation, Cellular Crosstalk, and Precision Intervention.
abstract: Poststroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) is a dynamic syndrome driven by focal brain injury, pre-existing cerebrovascular burden, metabolic comorbidities, and reduced brain resilience. Increasing evidence suggests that persistent disruption of redox-metabolic communication within the neurovascular unit (NVU), rather than neuronal loss alone, promotes the transition from acute ischemic injury to chronic cognitive decline. This review summarizes metabolic reprogramming in BMECs, pericytes, astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocyte-lineage cells, and neurons, emphasizing the intercellular transfer of metabolites, reactive oxygen and nitrogen species, oxidized lipids, extracellular vesicles, and mitochondria. We propose that PSCI develops through a spatiotemporally dysregulated continuum involving vascular injury, cell-specific metabolic remodeling, maladaptive signal propagation, impaired axonal and synaptic energy support, and progressive network disconnection. Ischemia-reperfusion triggers bioenergetic failure, NADH/NAD+ imbalance, mitochondrial electron leakage, endothelial dysfunction, and capillary no-reflow. Subsequently, blood-brain barrier disruption, immunometabolic activation, iron and lipid dysregulation, and defective organelle quality control sustain white matter and synaptic injury. Therapeutic strategies should therefore be stage-specific: restoring microcirculatory perfusion and physiological redox signaling acutely, promoting inflammation resolution and metabolic repair subacutely, and combining vascular-metabolic modulation with neurorehabilitation chronically. Future studies should integrate cell type-specific interventions, metabolic flux tracing, spatial multi-omics, and longitudinal cognitive assessments to establish causal donor-carrier-recipient-stage-outcome relationships.

title: Atypical Handedness in Eating Disorders: Laterality and Its Relation to Neurocognitive Functioning.
journal: European eating disorders review : the journal of the Eating Disorders Association
abstract: Atypical handedness is more frequent in psychiatric disorders of neurodevelopmental origin, but eating disorders are absent from meta-analyses. We examined its presence, specificity, familial aggregation and neurocognitive correlates. The Edinburgh Handedness Inventory was administered to 1093 patients with lifetime anorexia nervosa, 562 with another eating disorder, 34 unaffected sisters and 419 healthy participants. Interview (n = 1006) and self-report (n = 1461) versions were analysed separately and related, in direction and degree, to 13 neurocognitive measures. Patients with lifetime anorexia nervosa were less right-lateralised than controls (adjusted difference 5.85 points, p = 0.015; OR for non-right-handedness 1.76, p = 0.001). The excess was in mixed-handedness (20.8% vs. 11.2%), not left-handedness (4.0% vs. 3.6%). It did not differ between diagnoses (p = 0.68) or with age at onset, and was similar in unaffected sisters. Handedness was unrelated to all 13 neurocognitive measures. Atypical handedness in eating disorders consists of reduced consistency, not reversed direction, is not specific to anorexia nervosa, and was not associated with neurocognitive performance in the pre-specified analysis. Unaffected sisters resemble patients, although too few for inference. The findings are compatible with an early neurodevelopmental characteristic antecedent to onset, not an illness correlate.

title: Hidden Drowsiness in Wakefulness: Differences in Resting-State EEG Profiles in Natural Short Sleepers Versus Recommended Length Sleepers.
abstract: Chronic insufficient sleep affects cardiovascular, endocrine, immune and nervous systems and is linked to cognitive decline and increased mortality. Among habitual short sleepers, a subgroup known as natural short sleepers (NSS) report sleeping ≤ 6 h per night without experiencing subjective daytime dysfunction. However, discrepancies between subjective and objective markers of alertness raise questions about their true cognitive state. NSS have been described as high in behavioural activation, a phenotype overlapping with ADHD and mania in which dysregulation of resting-state brain arousal has been well documented. Despite these parallels, few studies have investigated the neurophysiological features of NSS. The current study examined resting-state EEG in NSS and recommended-length sleepers (RLS) during eyes-open conditions. Results showed that NSS exhibited significantly higher global alpha power and regionally steeper aperiodic exponents, particularly in occipital areas, both markers of increased drowsiness. Although global exponent values did not differ significantly, a significant Group × Region interaction was observed and NSS showed a trend toward increasing aperiodic exponents over time, suggesting less stable wakefulness under low-stimulation conditions. These findings point to subtle neurophysiological differences in NSS, raising the possibility that their perceived resilience to short sleep may mask underlying drowsiness.

title: Traditional Chinese Medicine Regulates Microglia for the Treatment of Alzheimer's Disease: A Paradigm Shift From Phenotypic Modulation to Metabolic Reprogramming and Molecular Regulation.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) remains the most prevalent neurodegenerative disorder, and current pharmacotherapies provide only limited symptomatic relief without meaningful disease modification. Microglia-mediated neuroinflammation is a central driver of AD progression, yet conventional research on traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) has largely framed its effects as M1/M2 phenotypic modulation. This descriptive framework cannot capture the high heterogeneity of microglia in vivo or identify direct molecular targets. Phenotypic modulation and metabolic reprogramming are mechanistically distinct: M1/M2-associated markers are phenotypic readouts, whereas metabolic reprogramming refers to the causal rewiring of glycolysis, oxidative phosphorylation/TCA-cycle flux, lipid metabolism, and mitochondrial dysfunction. Recent advances in single-cell/spatial transcriptomics, multiomics, chemical proteomics, structural biology, and genetic validation are driving a paradigm shift from phenotypic description toward molecular targeting by accelerating TCM target discovery and mechanistic dissection. To avoid overstating target specificity, we apply a three-level evidence framework-direct target, target-dependent, and pathway-dependent-and emphasize that molecular docking and network pharmacology are hypothesis-generating rather than direct target evidence. TCM-derived compounds and formulas regulate an interconnected microglial metabo-inflammatory network across four modules: metabolic enzymes (e.g., isocitrate dehydrogenase 1 (IDH1), multifunctional enzyme type 2 [MFE-2], glutaminase 1 [GLS1], hexokinase 2 [HK2], and phosphodiesterase 4B [PDE4B]), metabolic sensors (e.g., triggering receptor expressed on myeloid cells 2 [TREM2] and succinate receptor 1 [SUCNR1]), cell-fate regulators (e.g., ferroptosis and autophagy/mitophagy), and transcriptional/inflammatory execution nodes (e.g., peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor gamma [PPARγ], nuclear factor erythroid 2-related factor 2 [Nrf2], and NOD-like receptor family pyrin domain-containing 3 [NLRP3]). These modules are linked by reciprocal feedback rather than a unidirectional causal cascade. Targeted delivery systems further support translational development by overcoming the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and enabling microglial targeting. Future mechanism-oriented trials should use chemically standardized TCM products and integrate target-engagement biomarkers with pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) assessment to bridge preclinical and clinical research. Overall, precise intervention in the microglial metabo-inflammatory network represents a promising frontier for TCM modernization and next-generation AD therapeutics. Trial Registration: ClinicalTrials.gov identifier: NCT06534723; WHO ICTRP Primary Registry: ITMCTR2023000014.

title: Clinician-Selected Alteplase Dosing in Acute Ischemic Stroke: Treatment Patterns and Adjusted Outcomes in a Taiwanese Registry.
abstract: Clinicians sometimes administer alteplase doses below the guideline-recommended regimen in routine stroke care, yet the patient characteristics underlying these decisions and their relationship with outcomes remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to identify factors associated with clinician-selected alteplase dosing and to examine the relationship between dose category and clinical outcomes. We retrospectively studied 418 Taiwanese patients with acute ischemic stroke who received intravenous alteplase without endovascular thrombectomy between January 2017 and June 2022. Administered doses were categorized as low (0.46-0.64 mg/kg), medium (0.67-0.84 mg/kg), or standard (0.85-0.94 mg/kg). Multinomial logistic regression identified factors associated with clinician-selected dose, and logistic regression evaluated good 90-day functional outcome, defined as a modified Rankin Scale score of 0-2. Older age was independently associated with low-dose rather than standard-dose treatment (adjusted odds ratio [aOR] per year, 1.07; 95% confidence interval [CI], 1.04-1.09). Diabetes mellitus was associated with both medium-dose (aOR, 1.84; 95% CI, 1.02-3.29) and low-dose treatment (aOR, 2.71; 95% CI, 1.60-4.60). Good 90-day outcome occurred in 44.0%, 53.6%, and 67.9% of the low-, medium-, and standard-dose groups, respectively. However, dose category was not independently associated with good outcome after adjustment for baseline characteristics and prestroke antithrombotic therapy. Hemorrhagic outcome estimates were imprecise because symptomatic intracranial hemorrhage events were uncommon. Real-world alteplase dosing primarily reflected baseline patient risk profiles and treatment-selection patterns. Crude differences in 90-day functional outcome between dose groups were attenuated after adjustment and should therefore be interpreted as treatment-selection associations rather than causal treatment effects.

title: Localized Vasculogenic Reprogramming via Tissue Nano-Transfection Accelerates and Enhances Repair of Acellular Nerve Grafts.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
abstract: Peripheral nerve injuries (PNI) that require graft-based reconstruction often result in incomplete functional recovery, in part because current grafting approaches fail to rapidly restore the vascular support required for sustained axonal regeneration. Here, we introduce an in situ, non-viral strategy for localized reconditioning of the regenerative microenvironment using Tissue Nanotransfection (TNT)-mediated delivery of vasculogenic transcription factors Etv2, Fli1, and Foxc2 (EFF) at surgical coaptation sites. In vitro, EFF delivery induced early vascular-associated transcriptional programs and endothelial marker expression in a subset of transfected cells. In a mouse model of segmental sciatic nerve injury, repaired with acellular nerve allografts, TNT-EFF promoted axonal entry, vascular-associated remodeling, and transcriptional programs associated with reparative immune and tissue-remodeling responses. TNT-treated grafts showed improved functional recovery compared to graft-only controls, including increased muscle contractile strength and reduced denervation-associated muscle degeneration. Exploratory regional transcriptomic analysis identified vascular and tissue remodeling associated programs in proximal nerves segments and axonal repair and transport-associated programs in distal segments. Together, these findings support localized TNT-mediated treatment as a strategy for reconditioning the regenerative microenvironment of acellular nerve allografts and a broadly applicable molecular strategy to enhance regeneration in nerve repair and other ischemic injury settings.

title: Schwann cell targeted gene delivery in peripheral neuropathy models and non-human primates.
journal: Molecular therapy : the journal of the American Society of Gene Therapy
abstract: Gene therapy using recombinant adeno-associated viral (rAAV) vectors is a promising strategy for treating inherited demyelinating neuropathies such as Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease type 1X (CMT1X). Efficient and safe targeting of myelinating Schwann cells remains a key challenge for clinical translation. Here, we evaluated the safety, efficacy and scale-up potential of Schwann cell targeting by clinically relevant rAAVrh10 and rAAVrh74 vectors following lumbar intrathecal delivery in CMT1X mice and non-human primates (NHPs). Both rAAVrh10 and rAAVrh74 achieved efficient, dose-dependent biodistribution to the peripheral nerves with expression in Schwann cells driven by cell-specific promoter. In the Gjb1-null CMT1X mouse model, delivery of the therapeutic human GJB1 gene led to significant functional and morphological improvements, including increased grip strength, faster nerve conduction velocities, improved myelination and decreased inflammation. In NHPs, both serotypes demonstrated robust PNS biodistribution and Schwann cell targeting without adverse neurological effects, or liver toxicity related to therapeutic vectors. Overall, a single lumbar intrathecal injection of rAAVrh10 or rAAVrh74 enables efficient, dose-dependent Schwann cell transduction and therapeutic gene expression with functional benefit in the Gjb1- null demyelinating neuropathy mouse model, without toxicity in NHPs. This study supports the clinical translation of rAAV-mediated gene therapy targeting Schwann cells for treating CMT1X.

title: Complex Endovascular Repair for Genetically-Triggered Aortic Disease in Italy (CENTRAL Multicentric Registry).
journal: Journal of endovascular therapy : an official journal of the International Society of Endovascular Specialists
abstract: The role of fenestrated and branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) in patients with genetically triggered aortic disease and connective tissue disorders (CTDs) remains controversial due to concerns regarding long-term durability and disease progression. This multicenter study aimed to evaluate early and mid-term outcomes of F/BEVAR in patients with CTD treated for thoracoabdominal aortic aneurysms (TAAAs). This retrospective multicenter study included all consecutive CTD patients with genetically triggered aortic disease undergoing F/BEVAR for TAAA between 2013 and 2024 at 12 Italian centers. Primary endpoints were technical and clinical success, early and mid-term survival, and major adverse events (MAEs). Secondary endpoints included target vessel instability and the need for reintervention. Survival and freedom from adverse events were estimated using Kaplan-Meier analysis. A total of 45 CTD patients (62.2% male; mean age, 56.4 ± 11.7 years) were treated with F/BEVAR. Marfan syndrome was present in 80% of patients, and 68.9% were treated for post-dissection TAAA. Most patients presented with type II TAAA (91.1%), and 88.9% had undergone at least 1 prior aortic operation. Technical and clinical success were achieved in 86.6% and 82.2% of cases, respectively. Early mortality and MAEs occurred in 4.4% of patients. During a mean clinical follow-up of 35.0 ± 33.9 months, estimated overall survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 90.0%, 86.7%, and 79.2%, respectively, with no aorta-related deaths. At a mean imaging follow-up of 33.8 ± 32.2 months, target vessel patency was 98.8%. Target vessel instability occurred in 40% of patients, and 42.2% required 1 or more secondary interventions. Reintervention-free survival at 12, 24, and 36 months was 75.6%, 72.4%, and 59.0%, respectively. No baseline, anatomic, or procedural variable independently predicted late adverse outcomes. In this cohort of CTD patients, predominantly treated in complex redo settings, F/BEVAR demonstrated acceptable early and mid-term outcomes. Late adverse events and reinterventions were frequent but consistent with the natural history of CTD-related aortic disease and were not driven by identifiable baseline factors. These findings support the role of F/BEVAR as a valuable approach within a comprehensive, lifelong management strategy for CTD patients rather than as a definitive alternative to open surgery (OS).Clinical ImpactPatients with genetically triggered aortic disease often require multiple interventions throughout their lifetime because of the progressive nature of the underlying aortopathy. In this context, fenestrated/branched endovascular aortic repair (F/BEVAR) should not be considered an alternative to open surgery, but rather a complementary approach within the long-term management of these patients. This multicenter study provides one of the largest dedicated experiences with F/BEVAR in this challenging population, showing that acceptable early and mid-term outcomes can be achieved even in complex redo and post-dissection settings. These findings support the integration of endovascular techniques into individualized, lifelong aortic treatment strategies at experienced centers, acknowledging the need for continued surveillance and secondary interventions.

title: Implication of the ADCY1 Gene in Lithium Response in Bipolar Disorder by Genome-Wide Association Meta-Analysis.
abstract: Efforts to examine the influence of genetics in the efficacy of lithium using genome-wide association studies (GWAS) have identified several loci. Here, we report new cases and meta-analyses to combine previous efforts. We report data from 1259 participants with bipolar disorder (BD) recruited at University College London who had been treated with lithium. The data come from three waves of genotyping on different arrays. The GWAS data from each array was analysed separately and then meta-analysed with two published lithium response GWAS datasets. Post-GWAS analyses were conducted to examine lithium response heritability and its genetic correlations with other traits. We also attempted to replicate past polygenic risk scores (PRS) results. SNP rs116927879 (A/G) was associated with lithium response at a genome-wide significance level (p = 4.509 × 10-08) with a consistent effect across all cohorts. rs116927879 is located on chromosome 7 and maps to the protein-coding gene ADCY1 and two pseudo-genes, GTF2IP13 and SEPT7P2. The sQTL results suggested that rs116927879 genotypes may influence the splicing of ADCY1 across different brain regions. We estimated the SNP heritability (h2) for good lithium response as 20.3% and 15.6% for subjective/objective response definitions, respectively. We did not observe any genetic correlation or PRS association between the lithium response and schizophrenia or major depression disorder. However, we found weak evidence to suggest that males are more likely to be good responders. Our GWAS identifies a genome-wide significant finding and provides updated heritability estimates for lithium efficacy.

title: Improvement of right-sided spatial neglect after parietal continuous theta-burst stimulation: A single-case study.
abstract: Spatial neglect is a common, disabling consequence of brain injury. Most rehabilitation research targets left neglect, leaving treatment options for right-sided neglect after left hemisphere injury limited. Randomized controlled trials have shown that continuous theta-burst stimulation (cTBS) over the intact posterior parietal cortex reduces left-sided neglect and its impact on daily living. We investigated whether the same approach could improve subacute right-sided neglect. A patient with severe right neglect and right homonymous hemianopia following left hemisphere injury received cTBS over the right posterior parietal cortex more than four months post-onset. Neglect was assessed with line bisection, cancellation, reaction-time measures of alertness and spatial attention, and the Catherine Bergego Scale (CBS). Performance was stable across two baseline assessments. After stimulation, line bisection improved significantly, from one day after the first stimulation block through follow-up. CBS scores also improved, indicating functional gains in daily living. Cancellation performance and spatial attention reaction times were unaffected, although the visual field loss complicated their interpretation. Right parietal cTBS was associated with sustained improvements in line bisection performance and daily functioning in a stable right-sided neglect. cTBS may therefore also have therapeutic potential for spatial neglect following left-hemisphere damage, possibly through modulation of interhemispheric interactions.

title: Postoperative Acute Kidney Injury in Children Undergoing Major Non-Cardiac Surgery: Protocol for a Multicentre Study (POAKIDS).
abstract: Acute kidney injury (AKI) is associated with increased mortality and adverse long-term outcomes. Postoperative AKI is a common and recognised complication after surgery in adults. In children, AKI following paediatric cardiac surgery has been extensively studied. However, the incidence and characteristics of postoperative AKI after non-cardiac surgery in children remain poorly defined, with existing evidence largely derived from retrospective and single-centre studies. POAKIDS is an international, multicentre, prospective observational study including hospitalised children aged 0-16 years undergoing major non-cardiac surgery under general anaesthesia. Postoperative AKI will be defined according to the Kidney Disease: Improving Global Outcomes (KDIGO). The primary outcome is the incidence of postoperative AKI. Secondary objectives include evaluation of established and novel urinary biomarkers as predictors of postoperative AKI and exploration of perioperative potential predictors of renal injury. The maximal follow-up is seven postoperative days. Sample size is based on the incidence estimate, with a planned inclusion of 2000 patients. Data will be analysed using descriptive statistics, agreement analyses, and exploratory regression models. This study aims to provide robust prospective data on the incidence of postoperative AKI in children undergoing major non-cardiac surgery and to improve understanding of perioperative renal injury in this population. By combining standardised AKI definitions with systematic biomarker assessment, the results are expected to inform future preventive strategies and guide the design of interventional studies targeting postoperative renal injury in paediatric perioperative care.

title: Brain-derived exosomes mediate antibody-resistant PRV transmission and blood-brain barrier disruption.
abstract: Exosomes are critical mediators of virus-host interactions and can transfer viral and host components that influence viral replication and tissue injury. Pseudorabies virus (PRV), a neurotropic alphaherpesvirus, has been reported to disrupt the blood-brain barrier (BBB) and cause severe neurological disease. However, the role of exosomes in PRV-induced neuropathogenesis remains unclear. Here, we systematically investigated the functional role of brain-derived exosomes generated during PRV infection. Exosomes were isolated from PRV-challenged and mock-treated mouse brains using differential ultracentrifugation coupled with cluster of differentiation (CD)9-/CD63-/CD81-based immunomagnetic enrichment. Purity was confirmed by transmission electron microscopy, nanoparticle tracking analysis, and western blotting, which excluded intact virion contamination. Notably, multimarker enrichment yielded higher recovery than CD63 alone. PRV-associated exosomes contained viral genomic DNA and glycoproteins and mediated efficient viral transmission in porcine kidney (PK)-15 cells. In a Transwell-based BBB model composed of bEnd.3 endothelial cells and astrocyte type I clone (C8-D1A), these exosomes induced significant barrier dysfunction. Consistently, intracranial administration of exosomes from PRV-infected mice resulted in neurological deficits and increased BBB permeability in vivo. Together, our findings identify brain-derived exosomes as previously underappreciated mediators of PRV dissemination and neurovascular injury. These findings reveal an exosome-associated pathway that may contribute to PRV neuropathogenesis.

title: Modulation of lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181 and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1 signaling pathways in rotenone-induced neurodegeneration rat model.
abstract: Parkinson's disease (PD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder characterized by dopaminergic neuronal loss and α-synuclein-rich Lewy body accumulation. Mitochondrial dysfunction and microRNA (miRNA) dysregulation, particularly mitochondrial miRNAs (mitomiRs), are critical drivers of PD pathogenesis. This study investigated the neuroprotective efficacy of the SGLT2 inhibitor, dapagliflozin, against rotenone-induced neurotoxicity, focusing on the lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181/PTEN and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1/AMPK signaling axes. Male Wistar rats were randomized into three groups: a control group, a PD model group received rotenone (2 mg/kg every 48 h, s.c.), and a treatment group received rotenone plus dapagliflozin (10 mg/kg/day, p.o.) for 28 days. In the inducted rotenone group lincRNA-p21 sponges mir-181 which leads to the upregulation of PTEN which inhibits the conversion of PIP2 to PIP3 thus downregulating AKT expression and subsequent activation of GSK-3β kinase enzyme which increases α-synuclein accumulation. In addition, the PD-control group showed upregulation of Mitomir-23b with subsequent downregulation of SIRT-1 expression and inactivation of LKB1. Accompanied by inhibition of AMPK phosphorylation which in turn prevents the degradation of accumulated α-synuclein. Dapagliflozin treatment upregulates mir-181 and downregulates mitomir-23b, which restores DJ-1 levels, which in turn activate the antioxidant genes HO-1 and PINK1, and improve mitochondrial function. Dapagliflozin exerts neuroprotection by restoring lincRNA-p21/mitomiR-181/PTEN and mitomiR-23b/SIRT1/AMPK homeostasis, thereby inhibiting α-synuclein proteotoxicity and mitigating oxidative stress and neuroinflammation.

title: Muscarinic acetylcholine receptor M2 in the anterior cingulate cortex mediates central sensitization after peripheral nerve injury.
abstract: The activation of α-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor subunit glutamate A1 (GluA1) in anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) has been implicated mechanical sensitization after peripheral nerve injury. Separately, muscarinic acetylcholine receptor (mAChR) activation is known to initiate downstream signaling cascades that regulate glutamate receptor expression, trafficking, and upregulation. To investigate the role of mAChR in the ACC under neuropathic pain conditions, we employed chronic constriction injury (CCI) modeling combined with mechanical allodynia tests, in vitro whole-cell patch-clamp recordings, western blotting, immunofluorescence staining, and RNA interference techniques in this study. Our results demonstrated that CCI led to increased amplitude and frequency of miniature excitatory postsynaptic currents, along with elevated GluA1 protein levels in the ACC. Notably, expression of mAChR M2 in the ACC was not significantly altered following nerve injury. However, conditional knockdown of mAChR M2 in ACC excitatory neurons significantly reduced GluA1 expression and attenuated neuropathic pain development in mice. These results indicate that the activity of mAChRs M2 in ACC pyramidal neurons is necessary for GluA1-dependent synaptic strengthening and pain sensitization. Thus, targeting this receptor may represent a viable strategy for alleviating ACC-mediated chronic pain.

title: Data-driven clustering of atrophy patterns in Alzheimer's disease.
abstract: To enable early detection and treatment of Alzheimer's disease, a better understanding of the heterogeneous disease progression is needed. Longitudinal MRI data has been utilized by previous studies to uncover patterns of brain atrophy. In this work, we aimed to improve upon previous methods by combining a continuous modeling of disease stages with a data-driven clustering algorithm. We developed an algorithm that primarily stages subjects on a continuous latent-time disease scale and subsequently finds clusters of atrophy patterns in a completely data-driven manner. The core of the algorithm is a set of non-linear mixed-effects models, which includes both subject-specific random effects and cluster-specific fixed effects. We applied our algorithm to longitudinal MRI data from the ADNI and OASIS databases and analyzed the found clusters rigorously by studying biomarkers, indicators of co-pathologies, and connections with previously established subtypes. We also utilized the BioFINDER-2 cohort as an independent validation dataset. We found four clusters of longitudinal atrophy patterns; A: Progressive atrophy, B: Slow progression, C: Delayed atrophy and D: High atrophy. The D (High atrophy) exhibited higher amounts of atrophy, primarily in the typical regions affected in AD. The delayed atrophy group C remained relatively spared until the final stages of the disease, where we saw rapid neurodegeneration. The B (Slow progression) group displayed the least atrophy, and the A (Progressive atrophy) group showed a typical AD-like progression. However, the clusters could only be somewhat reproduced in perturbations of the discovery cohort. In the validation cohort, two clusters were found, which to a certain degree resembled some characteristics of the ADNI/OASIS clusters. Our method combines a continuous disease staging model with a data-driven clustering algorithm, which mitigates some limitations of previous attempts at modeling brain atrophy patterns in Alzheimer's disease. We found four clusters of atrophy patterns, which expressed different clinical profiles. However, the clusters are likely mixes of previously found AD subtypes, and are produced from continuous progression patterns rather than discrete subtypes.

title: Enhanced cognitive behavioural therapy for suicidality among people with comorbid mental and physical health conditions: study protocol of a pragmatic randomised controlled trial.
abstract: Suicidal behaviours represent significant public health concerns. People who present with suicidal ideation and/or self-harm are at an increased risk of suicide. The presence of co-existing or comorbid mental and physical health conditions, coupled with neurobiological factors, exacerbates mental health conditions and increases the risk of suicidal behaviours. Psychotherapeutic interventions, including Cognitive Behavioural Therapy, have been considered first line of treatment for several standalone and comorbid populations. However, research into CBT tailored for people at risk of suicide and self-harm while living with mental and physical health comorbidities is lacking. Therefore, this pragmatic trial aims to examine the effectiveness of an enhanced CBT in addition to standard care in reducing suicidal ideation, compared to standard care only. The study will follow a pragmatic randomised controlled trial design. The primary outcome is post-intervention severity of suicidal ideation and secondary outcomes include self-harm behaviours, depression and anxiety, coping, hopelessness, impact of comorbid conditions, and mental well-being. Additionally, blood and salivary samples will be collected to measure biomarkers of inflammation, hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal (HPA)- axis, neural plasticity, and the tryptophan-kynurenine pathway. Participants will be randomised following stratification and blocking into the intervention and control arm, and the data will be collected at baseline, post-intervention, and a 3-month follow-up. A participant safety plan specific to the project has been developed and will be implemented throughout the study duration. This protocol has been developed following the SPIRIT guidelines. People who live with long-term physical health conditions and co-existing depression, anxiety and distress are at increased risk of suicidal ideation and self-harm. Using a pragmatic randomised controlled trial methodology, the results of this study will contribute to improving our knowledge of implementing an evidence-based CBT intervention on suicidal ideation including self-harm behaviours, psychological state and biological factors. Prospectively registered on ISRCTN, ISRCTN17751649. Registered on 21 August 2024, https://doi.org/10.1186/ISRCTN17751649 .

title: Comparison of blood-brain barrier water exchange rate in young and older adults with diffusion-weighted and multi-echo arterial spin labeling MRI.
journal: Fluids and barriers of the CNS
abstract: Water exchange rate (Kw) across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) has emerged as a candidate biomarker for assessing aging and neurological disease. This work sought to compare the diffusion-weighted (DW) and multi-echo (ME) arterial spin labeling (ASL) MRI sequences that assess Kw across the BBB in a young and an older healthy cohort to examine Kw changes in different brain regions associated with age group. 12 young healthy (21-30 years, 26 ± 3 years, 8 female) and 18 older healthy (66-84 years, 75 ± 7 years, 13 female) participants underwent DW and ME ASL imaging along with structural T1-weighted scans on a 3T MRI. Kw, arterial transit time (ATT), and cerebral blood flow (CBF) maps were linearly registered to the structural images, which were then segmented using FreeSurfer into masks with 35 bilateral gray matter regions to extract regional Kw measures. Global and regional values were compared between younger and older participants using mixed-effect linear regression and two-sample t-tests with false discovery rate (FDR) correction. Additional linear regressions were utilized to directly correlate Kw, CBF, and ATT from the two ASL methods. DW and ME ASL produced opposite age-group differences in Kw in the whole brain and across all four lobes. Substantially higher absolute Kw values were observed using ME ASL compared to DW ASL. CBF exhibited a strong positive association (β = 1.15, p < 0.001) between DW and ME ASL while ATT showed a moderate positive relationship (β = 0.46, p < 0.001). Kw, on the other hand, was negatively associated (β = -0.62, p < 0.001) between the two ASL methods. ME ASL detected higher Kw in older adults within medial orbitofrontal, inferior frontal, anterior cingulate, inferior temporal, transverse temporal, sensorimotor, and insula regions. DW and ME ASL detected distinctive patterns of BBB Kw change between young and older adults, with ME ASL identifying a greater number of statistically significant regional age-group differences in this cohort. Discrepancy in absolute values suggest method-dependent differences in ASL-derived Kw estimates, in addition to opposite age-group trends. Further validation is needed to understand contexts in which DW ASL and ME ASL are interchangeable versus complementary quantitative markers of BBB water exchange.

title: Alterations in dopaminergic activity in the large intestine of horses with pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction.
abstract: Pituitary pars intermedia dysfunction (PPID) is a neurogenerative disorder in horses characterised by dopaminergic neuronal loss, resembling Parkinson's disease. While Parkinson's disease involves dopaminergic degeneration in both the brain and the gut, intestinal involvement in PPID has not been investigated. This study aims to investigate dopaminergic activity in the enteric nervous system (ENS) of the large intestine in horses with PPID. Archived intestinal samples from horses with PPID (pituitary grade 4/5 or 5/5 with clinical signs consistent with PPID) and aged controls (pituitary grade 1/5 or 2/5) were used. Expression of tyrosine hydroxylase (TH) and dopamine receptor-2 (D2R) were measured in the ENS of the caecum, large colon, and small colon by immunohistochemistry. Quantification of positive staining was performed on 8 ganglia per sample and averaged. Statistical comparisons were made using unpaired t-test or Mann-Whitney test for group difference, and one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) or Kruskal-Wallis test across intestinal segments. Horses with PPID showed significantly lower TH expressions in the submucosal plexus of the caecum (control vs. PPID: 1.97% [0-16.52] vs. 0.03% [0-0.46], P = 0.042), and significantly higher D2R expression in both the submucosal plexus (0.66% [0.04-1.23] vs. 3.86% [0.06-8.93], P = 0.011) and myenteric plexus (0.28% [0.03-2.34] vs. 1.50% [0.77-5.76], P = 0.045) of the caecum. These findings provide novel evidence of altered dopaminergic signalling in the equine gut in PPID, suggesting enteric involvement in disease pathophysiology. Further research into enteric glial function and D2R targeted therapies are warranted.

title: Weight-loss interventions in gastrointestinal and liver diseases: a narrative review of GLP-1 based therapies, bariatric surgery, and endoscopic approaches.
abstract: Obesity and metabolic dysfunction are increasingly prevalent in patients with diverse gastrointestinal and liver diseases and contribute to disease progression, treatment response, and long-term clinical outcomes. In parallel, the therapeutic landscape for obesity has expanded rapidly, with growing use of incretin receptor agonists (RA), including glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP1)-RA, bariatric surgery, and endoscopic bariatric therapies. Understanding how these weight-loss interventions influence gastrointestinal disease activity, safety, and malignancy risk is essential for clinical decision-making. This narrative review synthesizes current evidence on the effects of obesity as well as weight-loss therapies across a spectrum of gastrointestinal and liver conditions, including metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD), inflammatory bowel disease (IBD), gastroesophageal reflux disease, celiac disease, gastrointestinal malignancies, and dumping syndrome. We summarize data from randomized trials, observational cohorts, and meta-analyses evaluating clinical outcomes, disease activity, adverse events, and cancer risk. In MASLD, GLP1-RA and bariatric surgery improve hepatic steatosis and steatohepatitis without aggravation of fibrosis. Fibrosis outcomes are most strongly influenced by sustained weight loss and improvements in insulin resistance. In IBD, obesity (particularly increased visceral fat) may negatively impact response to biologics; however, observational data suggest that GLP1-RA are not associated with increased IBD disease activity and may be associated with favorable clinical outcomes in selected patients with obesity. Bariatric surgery-particularly sleeve gastrectomy-may improve IBD control in carefully selected patients. Data on endoscopic bariatric therapies in IBD are limited but may be effective in selected patients. Gastrointestinal malignancies have increased prevalence in obesity, including esophageal, pancreatic, liver, and colorectal cancers. Current randomized and observational data do not demonstrate consistently increased cancer risk with GLP-1 based therapies, while bariatric surgery may be associated with reduced risk of selected obesity-related cancers. Evidence linking endoscopic bariatric therapies to malignancy risk is currently lacking. Dumping syndrome is a complication of bariatric surgery, but has not been reported following endoscopic bariatric therapies, likely due to delayed gastric emptying. Collectively, weight-loss therapies are increasingly important in the management of gastrointestinal and liver diseases. Ongoing studies and longer-term follow-up are needed to clarify durability of benefit, procedure-specific risks, and optimal patient selection for GLP-1 based therapies.

title: Evaluation of Antiseizure Potential of Rufinamide and Celecoxib Combination in a PTZ-Kindled Mouse Model Through Electrophysiological, Neurobehavioral, and Molecular Analyses.
abstract: Pentylenetetrazole (PTZ)-induced kindling is a well-established experimental model for investigating epileptogenesis and evaluating the therapeutic potential of antiseizure drugs and their novel combinations. The current study investigated whether rufinamide (RUF) and celecoxib (CEL) administered individually and in combination during PTZ-kindling acquisition, attenuate seizure progression and associated neurobehavioral, biochemical, histopathological, and molecular alterations in PTZ-kindled mice. Male mice received 11 injections of PTZ at the dose of 40 mg/kg on alternate days along with daily treatment of RUF, CEL, or RUF + CEL throughout the 21-day kindling protocol. Seizure severity was monitored using behavioral seizure scoring and validated by electroencephalographic (EEG) recordings of cortical epileptiform activity. The results demonstrated that RUF alone and RUF + CEL combination versus PTZ-kindled mice significantly attenuated seizure progression and reduced epileptiform EEG discharges (p < 0.01). Behavioral assessments revealed that treated animals exhibited reduced anxiety-like behavior along with improved cognitive performance (p < 0.05-0.001). In addition, depression-like behavior evaluated by the sucrose preference test was significantly improved (p < 0.01). Biochemical analyses indicated reduced lipid peroxidation (MDA) and enhanced antioxidant defenses including SOD, GPx, and CAT, with normalization of AChE activity (p < 0.05). Furthermore, RUF and CEL treatment significantly downregulated the expression of TNF-α, IL-1β, and GFAP, indicating attenuation of neuroinflammatory responses. Histopathological outcomes further supported these findings, demonstrating preservation of neuronal architecture and increased neuronal persistence in the hippocampal subregions. Collectively, these findings suggest that the RUF + CEL combination provides enhanced protection against PTZ-induced epileptogenesis and its associated neurobehavioral and neuropathological alterations, potentially through complementary modulation of neuronal excitability, oxidative stress, and neuroinflammatory pathways.

title: Neuromodulation of cortical networks facilitates motor generalization of balance training in older adults.
abstract: Motor generalization, the ability to transfer learned motor skills to untrained contexts, declines with aging and limits the functional benefits of rehabilitation. Although transcutaneous vagus nerve stimulation (tVNS) has been implicated in neuroplasticity, its potential to facilitate motor generalization and associated cortical network reorganization in older adults remains unclear. Forty community-dwelling older adults (69.2 ± 4.3 years) were randomly assigned to receive either tVNS (n = 20) or sham stimulation (n = 20) during stabilometer balance training. Motor generalization was assessed on the day following training using an untrained foam-stance task. Postural regulation was characterized using center-of-pressure (COP) measures, stabilogram diffusion analysis, a composite control index (CCI), and sample entropy (SampEn). Cortical network organization was examined using beta-band electroencephalography (EEG) functional connectivity and minimum spanning tree (MST) analysis. Compared with sham stimulation, tVNS-assisted training produced greater improvements in COP area, accompanied by changes in postural dynamics, CCI, and SampEn. MST analyses revealed increased leaf fraction and reduced average eccentricity and network diameter, although baseline-adjusted analyses provided the most consistent support for average eccentricity. Exploratory correlations further showed that changes in average eccentricity were associated with changes in critical displacement and CCI after false discovery rate correction. These findings suggest that tVNS-assisted balance training may enhance short-term transfer of postural learning in older adults, accompanied by cortical network topology reorganization. The observed neural-behavioral associations support the functional relevance of network changes but do not establish a causal mediating mechanism.

title: Jujuboside A from Ziziphus: Chemistry, mechanistic pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and formulation roadmap toward neuroactive translation.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
abstract: Jujuboside A (JuA) is a dammarane-type triterpenoid saponin and a principal quality marker of Ziziphi spinosae semen (ZSS) and selected Ziziphus taxa. This review aimed to integrate current evidence on JuA chemistry, central nervous system (CNS) pharmacology, pharmacokinetics (PK), metabolism, safety, analytical standardization, and formulation strategies toward neuroactive translation. Evidence relevant to these domains was synthesized and critically organized to define the chemical, pharmacological, pharmacokinetic, quality-control, and formulation profile of JuA. JuA is characterized by a jujubogenin aglycone linked to a branched oligosaccharide chain, while comparative Ziziphus saponins, including JuB, JuC, protojujubosides, and jujubogenin, clarify how glycosylation influences amphiphilicity, stability, and disposition. Mechanistic evidence is strongest for CNS-related effects, particularly GABAergic modulation, neuroinflammatory restraint, mitochondrial and synaptic protection, and sleep- or stress-linked behavioral outcomes. JuA shows low oral exposure, with an oral bioavailability of approximately 1.32% and rapid stepwise deglycosylation to JuB and jujubogenin, supporting a metabolite-driven pharmacodynamic model. Standardization should integrate authenticated botanical sourcing, ultra-performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) or charged-aerosol detection/quantitative nuclear magnetic resonance (CAD/qNMR) quantification, chemometric fingerprints, and contaminant controls. Lipid-based systems, cyclodextrin complexes, and amorphous solid dispersions should be evaluated for their capacity to protect labile glycosidic linkages, sustain supersaturation, and improve exposure to pharmacologically relevant species. Key priorities are direct receptor engagement, brain-region exposure mapping, PK/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) alignment, standardized clinical-grade materials, and early human studies using objective sleep endpoints.

title: Drp-1 Participates in LPS-Induced Neuroinflammation and Microglia-Neuron Interaction Through mtDNA-cGAS-STING Axis.
abstract: To investigate the role of dynamin-related protein 1 (Drp-1) in the process of LPS-induced microglial injury and its initiated neuroinflammation. C57BL/6J mice or BV2 microglia were challenged with LPS, and the behavioral performance and the cell viability were tested, respectively. The expression of Drp-1, inflammatory factors, and key molecules of the cGAS-STING signaling pathway was measured in the mouse hippocampus or in microglia in vitro, together with the abundance of mtDNA. Moreover, the effect of Drp-1 was further explored by siRNA in vitro and its selective inhibitor Mdivi-1 in vivo. Furthermore, a co-culture system of microglia and neurons was used to observe the potential role of cell-free mtDNA in the microglia-neuron crosstalk. Meanwhile, the plasma levels of cell-free mitochondrial DNA (cf-mtDNA) were detected in patients with major depressive disorder (MDD). In vivo, intraperitoneal injection of LPS could result in anxious-like and depression-like behaviors in mice, together with a significant microglial activation and its related neuroinflammation, mtDNA release, and the imbalanced expression of synaptic plasticity, Drp-1, cGAS, STING, p-STING, and IRF3 in the hippocampus. All these behavioral and neuropathological changes could be reversed by treatment with Mdivi-1. Moreover, LPS-induced behavioral dysfunction and neuropathological injuries were also observed in mice that received hippocampal stereotactic injection of mtDNA. In vitro, besides the detrimental effect of LPS on microglia, our results indicated a crucial role of microglia-derived mtDNA in linking Drp-1-associated mitochondrial dysfunction to LPS-induced microglial injury and neuroinflammation, and in the crosstalk between HT22 and BV2 cells. Additionally, the plasma concentration of cf-mtDNA was increased in MDD patients, with a significant positive correlation with plasma levels of IL-6, IL-1β, TNF-α, and IFN-γ. As a key regulator of mitochondrial fission, the imbalanced expression of Drp-1 participates in LPS-induced microglial injury and neuroinflammation via the Drp-1-mtDNA-cGAS-STING axis.

title: A pilot randomized feasibility trial of perioperative melatonin for cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, sedative and analgesic medication use, and mechanical ventilation following CABG.
journal: Daru : journal of Faculty of Pharmacy, Tehran University of Medical Sciences
abstract: Perioperative complications remain common following coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). Although melatonin may have cardioprotective and sedative-sparing effects, its feasibility and potential effects on early postoperative cardiac rhythm and recovery in patients undergoing CABG remain unclear. To assess the feasibility of a future definitive randomized controlled trial (RCT) of perioperative melatonin in patients undergoing on-pump CABG and to obtain preliminary estimates of its effects on cardiac arrhythmias during cardiopulmonary bypass (CPB) weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. In this pilot randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled feasibility trial, 22 adults undergoing elective on-pump CABG were randomly assigned in a 1:1 ratio to receive oral melatonin (3 mg) or placebo nightly, from three nights before to three nights after surgery. Feasibility outcomes included recruitment, retention, protocol adherence, completeness of outcome assessment, and intervention safety. Exploratory clinical outcomes included cardiac arrhythmias during CPB weaning, duration of mechanical ventilation, and postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use. Twenty-two participants were randomized. The recruitment rate was 68.75%, while retention, protocol adherence, and completeness of outcome assessment were all 100%; no treatment-related adverse events were observed. Arrhythmias during CPB weaning occurred in 2 of 11 participants (18.2%) in each group (OR, 1.00; 95% CI: 0.11-8.73). The median duration of mechanical ventilation was 9.5 hours with melatonin and 15.0 hours with placebo (Hodges-Lehmann estimate of the between-group location shift, -3.30 hours; 95% CI: -6.90 to 1.05). Postoperative sedative and analgesic medication use was generally comparable between groups, although the corresponding effect estimates were imprecise. Melatonin was feasible and well tolerated in this pilot cohort, with no treatment-related adverse events observed. The exploratory estimates were imprecise and do not provide evidence of efficacy, supporting a larger, adequately powered randomized trial to further evaluate the efficacy and safety of melatonin. IRCT20250206064666N1, date of registration: 2025-02-24.

title: Rehabilitation Strategies for Upper Limb Function After Breast Cancer Treatment, with and Without Lymphedema: The Potential of Proprioceptive Neuromuscular Facilitation - A Systematic Review.
abstract: Upper limb dysfunction (pain, reduced shoulder mobility and strength, activity limitation) is common after breast cancer treatment, with or without breast cancer-related lymphedema (BCRL). Proprioceptive neuromuscular facilitation (PNF) has been proposed to improve upper limb function and range of motion (ROM). This systematic review evaluates PNF for upper limb dysfunction in women treated for breast cancer, analyzing women with and without BCRL separately. The Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) 2020 statement was followed. Four databases were searched without date restrictions. Randomized or quasi-randomized English-language trials of PNF-containing interventions in women treated for breast cancer were included. Risk of bias was assessed with the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool and certainty of evidence with the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development and Evaluation (GRADE) approach. Six trials (366 women) were included: three enrolled women with confirmed BCRL and three women without BCRL. PNF was mostly part of multimodal programs, but the between-group contrast isolated PNF in four trials. In BCRL trials, limb volume decreased in all groups, with no consistent advantage of PNF over active comparators. In women without BCRL, single trials reported improvements in ROM, strength and function. Risk of bias was low in one trial, high in one and of some concern in four; certainty of evidence was low or very low. PNF may be a promising component of multimodal rehabilitation for upper limb dysfunction after breast cancer treatment; its independent effectiveness and its effects on BCRL remain unproven, and in women with BCRL it should complement, not replace, decongestive treatment. Trials in women with confirmed BCRL and standardized PNF protocols are needed. PROSPERO CRD42025641774, registered on 2 February 2025 (retrospectively registered).

title: Functional signatures of preclinical diabetic retinal neurodegeneration without clinically detectable retinopathy: a combined mfERG and mfPOP study.
journal: Graefe's archive for clinical and experimental ophthalmology = Albrecht von Graefes Archiv fur klinische und experimentelle Ophthalmologie
abstract: To compare multifocal electroretinography (mfERG) and multifocal pupillographic objective perimetry (mfPOP; ObjectiveFIELD Analyzer [OFA]) in type 2 diabetic eyes without clinically detectable retinopathy (noDR), focusing on diagnostic performance, regional concordance, and short-term repeatability. Twenty noDR eyes and twenty age-, sex-, and laterality-balanced controls underwent ISCEV-standard mfERG and OFA 10 ETDRS (M18) testing. Outcomes were analysed across foveal, parafoveal, and perifoveal zones. Between-group comparisons used t tests or Mann-Whitney U tests with false discovery rate correction. ROC analysis with zone-matched DeLong tests assessed diagnostic performance; Spearman correlations assessed cross-modality concordance, and Bland-Altman analysis and intraclass correlation coefficients (ICCs) assessed same-day OFA repeatability. OFA global sensitivity and delay indices and zonal total-deviation measures were significantly abnormal in noDR eyes across all three zones. mfERG RMS and P1 amplitudes were reduced across all zones, while P1 implicit time was prolonged at the fovea and parafovea. mfERG P1 implicit time showed higher parafoveal discrimination than OFA Delay TD (p = 0.039), whereas OFA Delay TD showed higher perifoveal discrimination (p = 0.034); no significant modality differences occurred at the fovea or in sensitivity-domain comparisons. None of nine zone-matched OFA-mfERG correlations was significant within the noDR group. OFA Sensitivity MD and Delay MD showed excellent same-day repeatability (ICC = 0.980 and 0.984). mfERG and mfPOP detect region-dependent functional abnormalities in type 2 diabetic eyes without clinically detectable retinopathy. In this exploratory pilot comparison, limited within-group concordance raises the possibility that the two modalities capture partly distinct information. Larger longitudinal studies are needed to determine their prognostic value.

title: A two-platform blueprint for modeling human brain development.
abstract: No single experimental system spans human neural-plate induction through late-stage circuit maturation. Brain organoids have transformed human developmental neuroscience, yet a decade of progress has clarified their intrinsic limitations: they cannot fully recapitulate neural induction driven by embryo-scale developmental signals, nor achieve the degree of circuit maturation that requires an in vivo physiological context. Stem cell-based embryo models are positioned to provide mechanistic access to peri-gastrulation and early neurulation, whereas interspecies chimeras provide the physiological milieu to study myelination, pruning and circuit-level function. Here we propose a two-platform roadmap that integrates stem cell-based embryo models to decode developmental logic with interspecies chimeras to study functional maturation. We outline reproducibility and reporting standards, including rigorous benchmarks for neural-tube formation and closure, and present a milestone-based oversight framework anchored to verifiable developmental landmarks. Together, these complementary platforms enable causal interrogation of human neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative disease while remaining responsive to ethical and technical constraints.

title: Author Correction: Publisher Correction: Reactive oxygen species regulate axonal regeneration through the release of exosomal NADPH oxidase 2 complexes into injured axons.
The impact of anti-rhGAA antibody dynamics on functional outcomes in late-onset Pompe disease: insights from the French Pompe Registry.
abstract: The immune response to enzyme replacement therapy (ERT) in Pompe disease leads to the development of anti-drug antibodies; however, evidence of its impact on disease progression in adult patients remains unclear. In this retrospective cohort study, we examined the clinical progression of adult patients with late-onset Pompe disease (LOPD) registered in the French Late-Onset Pompe Disease registry who began alglucosidase therapy after age 18 and subsequently developed antibodies against recombinant human alpha-glucosidase (rhGAA). Patients were classified according to the maximum antibody titer observed during follow-up in subgroups: low (0-1:800), intermediate (1:1,600-1:12,800), and high (1:25,600-1:819,200). The main clinical outcomes utilized in our study were forced vital capacity (FVC) and the 6-min walking test (6MWT). A total of 160 patients were included in our study and were followed for a median of 5.9 years. Roughly a third of these patients (31%) exhibited a multiphasic immune response in anti-rhGAA titers. At baseline, ventilatory and ambulatory status differed across titer groups, with high-titer patients more likely to require invasive ventilation (p<0.001) and wheelchair assistance (p=0.036). Longitudinal mixed-effects analyses detected no statistically significant differences in FVC or 6MWT trajectories among the subgroups. In a landmark survival analysis, time to change in ambulation status was significantly shorter in the high-titer group (p=0.006). Longitudinal analyses on FVC and 6MWT trajectories did not reveal a significant difference among the titer groups.
