However, the landmark analysis identified earlier loss of ambulation among high-titer patients. Anti-rhGAA titers vary substantially, with multiphasic patterns observed in approximately one-third of patients.

title: Two maps chart Parkin's path from mutation to disease.
Functional atlas of Parkin predicts variant pathogenicity and Parkinson's disease age at onset.
abstract: Autosomal recessive mutations in the Parkin gene (PRKN) cause early-onset Parkinson's disease (PD). Parkin functions as a ubiquitin E3 ligase acting downstream of the PINK1 kinase to promote phosphorylated ubiquitin at sites of mitochondrial damage. Yet the functional effects of most PRKN gene variants remain unknown. Here, we use a pooled cellular assay measuring phosphorylated ubiquitin accumulation to quantify the activity of ~9200 PRKN missense and nonsense variants. Our screen identifies thousands of loss- and gain-of-function variants, including activating variants mainly residing at autoinhibitory interfaces. Functional scores accurately distinguish known PD pathogenic and benign variants, providing evidence of pathogenicity or benignity for 175/182 variants of uncertain significance (VUS). When combined into biallelic genotype scores, these data predict the age at disease onset in patients, revealing a quantitative link between Parkin activity and clinical manifestation. Our results provide a comprehensive functional genetic map of Parkin and demonstrate the power of multiplexed assays of variant effects (MAVEs) for variant interpretation and precision medicine in PD.

title: Dynamic visualization of cell adhesion molecule interactions using reversible split-HaloTag labeling in living cells.
abstract: Critical for diverse cellular functions, cell adhesion molecules (CAMs) interact to transduce information from the external environment to drive coordinated intracellular responses. However, direct visualization of CAM interactions in living cells and organisms remains a major challenge. Recent developments in split-HaloTag technology present a promising strategy for chemical labeling of protein-protein interactions. Here, we apply this method to dynamically monitor CAM interactions in living HEK293T cells using split-HaloTag-CAM fusion proteins. With high specificity, we visualized trans-cellular interactions between known adhesion pairs natively found in neuronal and immunological synapses. To expand the system's versatility, we adapted a modified split-HaloTag component (cpHaloΔN272H) that enables reversible dye exchange and facilitates rapid time-lapse imaging of CAM interactions. Leveraging fluorogenic HaloTag dyes, split-HaloTag-CAMs measured the real-time disassembly and reassembly of Ca2+-dependent CAM junctions in live cells. These tools enabled imaging long-term changes in surface contacts mediated by CAM binding, thus providing a robust platform for dissecting the spatiotemporal dynamics of CAM interactions in cellular and organismal contexts.

title: Ketamine promotes strategic and efficient approach-avoidance conflict resolution.
abstract: Adaptive behavior requires flexibly balancing approach and avoidance in risky or threatening environments, a flexibility disrupted in depression and other disorders marked by excessive avoidance. Benzodiazepines such as lorazepam broadly dampen neural excitability and synaptic plasticity, whereas ketamine may enhance both. We therefore asked whether ketamine promotes more strategic and efficient motivational behavior. In this completed randomized crossover study, 34 healthy participants with no lifetime neurological or psychiatric disorders and no regular medication use were assessed at the University Medical Center Freiburg (DRKS00025471). Participants completed three visits separated by seven days: a control visit without medication, followed by intranasal ketamine (50 mg) and oral lorazepam (1 mg) in randomized, counterbalanced order. Threat probability and loss magnitude were varied independently in a dynamic approach-avoidance conflict task conducted after ketamine's acute dissociative phase. Reported behavioral outcomes were net token gain, approach behavior, and approach and withdrawal latencies. Behavioral assessors were blinded to condition; participants and physicians were not. Mixed-effects models were used. All 34 randomized participants completed each condition and were analyzed. Ketamine yielded 57% higher token gains than control (β = 0.09, 95% confidence interval 0.05 to 0.13; p < 0.001) and 33% higher gains than lorazepam (β = 0.05, 0.01 to 0.09; p = 0.009). Behavior following ketamine was more strongly guided by outcome value than threat probability and showed faster approach and withdrawal responses. Lorazepam produced a less selective increase in approach behavior. No unexpected adverse events occurred. In healthy participants, ketamine was associated with more efficient and value-sensitive approach-avoidance behavior than control and lorazepam.

title: The strategic role of large-scale networks in advancing brain research societies.
The ZJU index as a novel predictive tool for post-stroke cognitive impairment: a prospective cohort study.
abstract: The ZJU index serves as a composite metabolic biomarker associated with metabolic dysregulation. Its relationship with post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) remains unestablished. This study aims to elucidate the association between ZJU index and PSCI incidence. We enrolled 261 patients with acute mild ischemic stroke. PSCI was defined as Mini-Mental State Examination < 27 at the 6-12 months follow-up. We collected clinical and laboratory data and calculated the ZJU index at baseline. ZJU index was dichotomized according to the prespecified cut-off points 36.13 for the high and low groups. Binary logistic regression and linear regression analyses were performed to analyze the association between ZJU index and cognitive outcomes. Predictive models incorporating ZJU index as continuous or categorical variables were developed, and a nomogram was constructed and validated. Bootstrap internal validation was performed to correct for optimism. The results revealed that ZJU index was significantly higher in the PSCI group. Higher ZJU index was an independent risk factor for PSCI (OR = 1.104, 95% CI = 1.032-1.181, P = 0.004) and associated with worse cognitive functions. The model using ZJU index as a continuous variable showed good discrimination (AUC = 0.736, 95% CI = 0.660-0.807), outperforming the categorical model (AUC = 0.709, 95% CI = 0.645-0.774) according to the net reclassification improvement and integrated discrimination improvement value. Bootstrap internal validation confirmed model stability (optimism‑corrected AUC = 0.711, 95% CI = 0.690-0.720). In conclusion, elevated ZJU index is independently associated with PSCI and may serve as a practical tool for early risk stratification.

title: Brain-state dependence of neuromodulation: psychosocial stress aligns prefrontal perfusion dynamics during online tDCS.
abstract: Transcranial direct current stimulation (tDCS) shows broad therapeutic promise, yet high inter-individual variability limits its clinical efficacy. Here, we investigated whether pre-stimulation brain state reduces inter-individual variability in neural responses to online tDCS. Across two sham-controlled cohorts of healthy volunteers, we quantified cerebral blood flow (CBF)-based inter-subject correlation (ISC) during 20 minutes of active or sham tDCS (anodal left dorsolateral prefrontal cortex, right supraorbital return). In our hypothesis-driven ROI analyses, following psychosocial stress induction (Study 1, N = 42; NCT07406503), active tDCS significantly synchronized perfusion trajectories (elevated ISC) within prefrontal and corresponding electric-field regions, while reducing synchrony in the pregenual anterior cingulate cortex. Crucially, this stress-dependent synchronization was absent during resting-state stimulation without prior stress exposure (Study 2, N = 43; NCT07406464). Exploratory whole-brain voxel-wise ISC and neurotransmitter-map association analyses further suggested that stress-state ISC modulations were preferentially aligned with normative cortical distributions of dopaminergic, noradrenergic, serotonergic, and GABAergic receptors, whereas such associations were not observed in the cohort without experimental stress induction. Although imaging modality differences (ASL vs. BOLD-fMRI) preclude attributing these divergences solely to stress, our findings demonstrate that psychosocial context shapes tDCS-induced neural synchrony, with exploratory evidence linking these effects to cortical neurotransmitter landscapes, providing a critical biological framework for state-sensitive and personalized psychiatric neuromodulation.

title: Biosynthesis of iboga alkaloids.
abstract: Tabernanthe iboga (iboga) is the source of voacangine, which is widely used as a semi-synthetic starting material for the anti-addiction agent ibogaine. Despite extensive investigation of voacangine biosynthesis, production of this compound cannot be reconstituted in a heterologous host, suggesting that one or more enzymes required for biosynthesis are missing. Additionally, T. iboga produces ibophyllidine, a pyrroloindole alkaloid that utilizes the same upstream precursor as voacangine, but is a member of a structurally distinct alkaloid class. Here we use bulk and single cell gene expression from leaf and root tissue to identify the unknown enzymes from these two pathways. We identify two additional enzymes that enable biosynthesis of voacangine in a heterologous host. The missing enzymes includes a pathogenesis-related (PR)10 family protein that likely catalyzes cyclization of a transient intermediate. Careful analysis of gene expression profiles in leaf and root also enabled the discovery of four additional enzymes that convert an upstream intermediate to ibophyllidine. This work reveals the chemical logic that generates two distinct alkaloid scaffolds in this important medicinal plant.

title: Addressing Inconsistency in Functional Neuroimaging: A Replicable Data-Driven Multi-Scale Functional Atlas for Canonical Brain Networks.
abstract: The advent of multiple neuroimaging methodologies has greatly aided in the conceptualization of large-scale functional brain networks in the field of cognitive neuroscience. However, there is inconsistency across studies in both nomenclature and the functional entities being described. There is a need for a unifying framework that standardizes terminology across studies while also bringing analyses and results into the same reference space. Here we improve the accessibility of a previously developed whole-brain template of canonical functional brain networks, expanding it into a powerful atlas, by manually labeling, organizing, and describing these networks with terms familiar to the fields of cognitive and affective neuroscience. These data-driven functional networks were developed by utilizing more than 100,000 resting-state fMRI datasets and are highly replicable across individual subjects and datasets and capture information from multiple spatial scales. The current report seeks to help optimize the utility of this atlas in future neuroimaging analyses by enhancing the comparability and easing the interpretation of new findings. The benefits of this atlas are not limited to future template-based or reference-guided analyses, but also extend to other data-driven neuroimaging approaches across modalities, such as those using blind independent component analysis (ICA). Future studies utilizing this atlas will contribute to greater harmonization and standardization in functional neuroimaging research.
